plan.title: Genotype x treatment interaction in KO vs WT brain RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is an interaction question on a balanced 2x2 factorial: genotype (WT, KO) x treatment (vehicle, drug), 4 biological replicates per cell, 16 samples in metadata.csv against 17 columns in counts.csv (gene-symbol column plus 16 sample columns), 12,000 genes, raw integer counts from salmon, human brain tissue. The plan therefore fits a single DESeq2 negative-binomial model with the design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, with WT and vehicle set explicitly as reference levels, and tests the interaction coefficient (genotypeKO.treatmentdrug) with the Wald test. That coefficient is the direct answer: it is the difference between the drug-vehicle effect in KO and the drug-vehicle effect in WT. Because a difference of differences carries roughly double the standard error of a simple effect, with n=4 per cell the interaction test is the least powered contrast in the design; the plan states this up front and requires the report to say so rather than reading a null interaction as evidence of no difference.

Order of work: T1S1 runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to check that the four cells separate as expected and that no sample is an outlier before any model is fit — the profile flags no batch variable and no quality concerns, so this step is a check rather than a correction. T1S2 fits the model once and extracts three result tables side by side for every gene: the drug effect within WT (the treatment main effect at the reference genotype), the drug effect within KO (main effect plus interaction, as a named contrast), and the interaction contrast itself. Shrinkage uses ashr rather than apeglm because two of the three reported effects are contrasts, not single model coefficients, and apeglm accepts only a coefficient. BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05 is applied within each contrast, and the p-value histogram is inspected before the adjustment is trusted. T1S3 re-fits the same design with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as an independent method and reports the overlap on the interaction contrast; the intersection is the high-confidence set. T2S1 runs preranked fgsea per contrast on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed ranking-metric choice is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic, which scales effect by uncertainty and does not saturate into ties), against human hallmark gene sets first and human Reactome pathways second, on the full ranked list of tested genes. Human collections are correct here — the data are Homo sapiens. T1S4 assembles the report.

Two honest caveats are built into the plan rather than left to the write-up. First, 12,000 genes is a reduced feature space for a human transcriptome, so the tested universe is not the whole annotated genome and the enrichment universe must be the tested genes only. Second, gene identifiers are symbols; symbol-to-Entrez mapping loss must be quantified and reported, and identifier spaces must not be mixed between the ranked list and the gene sets.

steps.name: Interaction report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the evidence that the drug acts differently in KO than in WT, and how strong is it given 4 replicates per cell?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Present, for every gene, the drug effect in WT, the drug effect in KO, and the interaction contrast side by side, naming WT and vehicle as the reference levels. Lead with the interaction result — the direct answer — then the two simple effects that give it meaning. Include the MA plot and dispersion plot from T1S2, the p-value histograms, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S3, and the per-contrast GSEA tables with leading-edge genes from T2S1. Record the method, package versions, design formula, every contrast, thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12,000, the number of significant genes per contrast, the gene-set collections with their versions, the random seeds, and full session information.
steps.context: The synthesizing document for the research question. It must not read a non-significant interaction as proof of no genotype-dependent drug effect, and must not read a gene significant in one genotype but not the other as proof of one.
acceptance_criteria: Gene tables give the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, and lfcSE, with genes ranked and plotted on the shrunken value
Reference levels (genotype = WT, treatment = vehicle) named beside every table
The three results — drug effect in WT, drug effect in KO, interaction contrast — presented side by side per gene
MA plot and dispersion plot placed before the gene tables, each with a one-line statement of what it shows
DESeq2/edgeR intersection reported as the high-confidence interaction set, with method-exclusive genes listed separately
Enrichment section states the collection, its version, the Wald-statistic ranking metric, the universe (tested genes), and the 15-500 size window
Report states explicitly that a null interaction at n=4 per cell is consistent with low power and is not evidence of equivalence
Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, seeds, gene-set collection versions
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit
Report the FDR as holding within each contrast, not across the three contrasts
State the enrichment result as method-dependent and hypothesis-generating
caveats: Do not describe a gene as showing a genotype-dependent drug effect on the basis of differing simple-effect significance alone — only the interaction contrast tests that claim
No transcript-length offsets were available for these salmon-derived gene-level counts; note the limitation in the methods section

grounding.reason: Report content for an interaction design follows R-0092 (simple effects beside the interaction contrast), R-0085/R-0087 (effect columns and fit diagnostics), R-0041/R-0051/R-0086 (method, thresholds, collection versions, reproducibility record).
